brief: Core Scientific registered a $1.3bn, 341,326 sq ft data center shell in Quinlan, Hunt County, Texas for AMD, with construction listed to start November 24, 2026, eight weeks before governor-elect Hinojosa's January 19, 2027 inauguration. Hinojosa campaigned on freezing new data center approvals and has since said the moratorium covers "all permits," while also saying she cannot revoke permits already granted. This building has its power agreement, land, tenant and most permits, but its backup-generator air permits are still pending at TCEQ, which Governor Abbott ordered to stop issuing data center permits on September 21 and which answers to Hinojosa from January. Wall Street has assumed projects already under construction are safe: Morgan Stanley, Bernstein and Goldman all size Texas risk by excluding under-construction capacity, which trackers define loosely enough to include land-clearing without an air permit. GLJ's Gordon Johnson says projects with power, permits and steel proceed; those missing environmental permits slip 12-18 months, which would push this building's planned September 2028 completion into late 2029 and pressure the bonds financing it. The moratorium wave is spreading to Arizona, Georgia, Ohio, Michigan and Minneapolis. The author expects the shell to be built but the generator permit, and the under-construction assumption, to be the real test.
